ai.title: Increase subscription credits for tier 100 and 500
ai.summary: Tier 100 creditsPerBlock increased from 350 to 420, and weeklyCreditsLimit from 3500 to 4200. Tier 500 creditsPerBlock increased from 2800 to 2940, with weeklyCreditsLimit raised to 29400. Changes applied to common/src/constants/subscription-plans.ts. Web pricing display updated in web/src/app/pricing/pricing-client.tsx to reflect adjusted usage multipliers.

eli5.text: If you pay for the $100 or $500 monthly plan, you now get more credits each week to use the assistant - the $100 plan went up by about 20% and the $500 plan by about 5%. You'd see these larger numbers when you check your usage on the pricing page. The change is live today.

ai.title: Hide ads for CLI subscribers
ai.summary: CLI now gates Gravity ads and slash commands for users with active subscriptions. `useGravityAd` accepts an `enabled` flag, while `chat.tsx` and `help-banner.tsx` use `useSubscriptionQuery` to determine visibility. Subscribers see no `/ads:enable` or `/ads:disable` prompts, and the help banner omits ad-related shortcuts.

eli5.text: If you have an active subscription, the program now hides promotional messages and the /ads commands that let you turn ads on or off. The subscription check happens automatically, so subscribers see a cleaner experience with fewer prompts. For people without a subscription, nothing changes and ads still appear as before.

ai.title: Disable Claude OAuth via feature flag
ai.summary: Added CLAUDE_OAUTH_ENABLED=false in common/src/constants/claude-oauth.ts to disable Claude OAuth functionality. This flag gates the /connect:claude command, OAuth banners, usage display, background credential refresh, and SDK direct Anthropic API routing. When disabled, /connect:claude shows a system message directing users to /subscribe.

eli5.text: If you work with Claude inside the terminal, the /connect:claude shortcut you may have seen is now switched off. Instead of opening a sign-in window for Claude, you will get a message telling you to use /subscribe, which is the new way to pay for usage across all models. This is now live today for the command line tool, so anyone typing /connect:claude will hit that message instead of the login flow.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.623 release bumps CLI version from 1.0.622
ai.summary: This release bumps the CLI package version in `cli/release/package.json` from 1.0.622 to 1.0.623. The version bump rolls up three user-visible changes shipped since 1.0.622: higher subscription credit tiers for tiers 100 and 500, ad-free CLI experience for subscribers via `useSubscriptionQuery` gating, and Claude OAuth disabled behind the `CLAUDE_OAUTH_ENABLED=false` flag in `common/src/constants/claude-oauth.ts`. No code logic changes occur in this commit itself; it solely advances the version to package the prior changes.
ai.evidence: The commit modifies `cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the `codebuff` package version from 1.0.622 to 1.0.623 (+1/-1).

eli5.text: This release upgrades the AI coding agent you use in your terminal and adds several quality-of-life improvements for people who pay for premium access. If you have a paid subscription, ads are now hidden from your chat and help screens so you can focus without interruptions, and the new code-editing tools let the agent make smoother, smarter updates to your files. Users on the highest subscription tiers get 20% more compute credits each week, so they can run longer or more complex tasks before hitting their allowance. The benchmark used to test and compare AI models was also switched to match the latest deep reasoning model variant. Finally, the old way of connecting your account through Claude's login flow has been turned off, with anyone trying it now directed to sign up for a paid plan instead.

ai.title: base-deep agent adopts 8-phase iterative workflow
ai.summary: agents/base2/base-deep.ts replaces loose orchestration instructions with a strict 8-phase workflow: Context, Deep Dive, Spec, Plan, Implement, Review, Validate, Lessons. Each phase enforces iterative critique loops using thinker-codex and code-reviewer-codex until no new issues arise. Implementation tasks now require writing SPEC.md, PLAN.md, and LESSONS.md to .agents/sessions/, updating .agents/skills/ with learnings.

eli5.text: The AI agent now follows a strict eight-step process when building something new: first it researches the code, then asks you questions, writes a spec document, makes a plan, writes the code, reviews it, tests it, and records lessons learned. Each step is defined and enforced, replacing the previous loose approach. If you ask it to implement a feature, you'll notice it takes a more structured, methodical approach with documentation saved along the way.

ai.title: Consolidate deep agent workflow into 7 phases
ai.summary: Reduced the `base-deep` agent workflow from 8 to 7 phases by merging the standalone Deep Dive into the Spec phase. The new Phase 2 requires drafting a `SPEC.md` before iterative `ask_user` refinement, followed by a `thinker-codex` critique loop. Added explicit two-phase todo tracking: planning todos (Phases 1-3) written at start, replaced by implementation todos after Phase 3. Updates `agents/base2/base-deep.ts` prompts, system instructions, and step reminders to reflect the condensed sequence.

eli5.text: The assistant now builds features in 7 steps instead of 8 by combining two earlier steps, writing a plan and asking you questions, into one. If you watch it work, you'll see it draft a spec document first and then ask you to refine it in one phase, followed by a single set of implementation tasks written up after planning is done. This affects anyone the assistant helps build code for, and it's live today in the version dated 2026-03-02.
